stem: A 19-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes misses several insulin doses and develops abdominal pain, deep respirations, and an anion-gap metabolic acidosis. Which of the following shifts in fuel use is associated with ketone production?

options.label: A
options.text: Greater use of fat rather than glucose for energy
options.misconception: None; this is the source-supported fuel shift associated with ketone formation.
options.explanation: When glucose cannot be used effectively, the body uses fat for energy, and that process produces ketones.

options.label: B
options.text: Greater storage of glucose as muscle glycogen
options.misconception: A glucose-storage pathway is being substituted for the alternative fuel use described in DKA.
options.explanation: Storing glucose as glycogen does not describe the shift toward fat use that accompanies ketone production.

options.label: C
options.text: Greater incorporation of amino acids into protein
options.misconception: An anabolic protein-building process is being confused with the alternative fuel pathway that produces ketones.
options.explanation: Protein synthesis does not account for the switch from glucose toward fat as an energy source.

options.label: D
options.text: Greater storage of triglyceride in adipose tissue
options.misconception: Energy storage is being selected instead of the increased use of fat that produces ketones.
options.explanation: Storing triglyceride does not describe the increased use of fat as an alternative energy source.

options.label: E
options.text: Greater uptake of glucose by peripheral tissues
options.misconception: Effective glucose use is being selected even though the vignette describes severe insulin deficiency.
options.explanation: Greater peripheral glucose uptake does not describe the cited shift toward fat use and ketone formation.

context: Learning objective: recognize the fuel shift associated with ketone production. When DKA develops, fuel use shifts toward fat, and ketones are produced during that shift.
